objectives: Use diagnostic evidence to select a specific fl-cycle skill for practice.
Re-teach the diagnosed component with explicit modelling and guided feedback.
Demonstrate transfer on 15 fresh reassessment items.
Advance only at or above 80%; continue targeted support below threshold.
concepts: Remediation should match the diagnosed component.
Recognition errors need listening contrasts; decoding errors need blending practice.
Encoding errors need segmentation and grapheme mapping; comprehension errors need text evidence.
Fresh reassessment checks transfer after teaching.

definitions.definition: Focused teaching and practice for a diagnosed learning need.
A new assessment after targeted instruction.
A fresh example used to check whether a skill generalises.

workedExamples.solution: Model /f/ /l/ smoothly, use sound boxes, then decode fresh fl-words.

workedExamples.prompt: A learner writes flag as fag.
workedExamples.solution: Segment the word, map f-l-a-g, then read it back.

workedExamples.prompt: A learner cannot answer where the flag is.
workedExamples.solution: Reread the sentence, locate “on the mat,” and use it as evidence.

commonMistakes: Repeating every lesson instead of targeting the diagnosed component.
Using speed alone as evidence of fluency.
keyTakeaways: Model, practise with feedback, then reassess with fresh items.
Use sound or text evidence to explain corrections.
revisionPoints: Decoding: blend every phoneme in order.
Encoding: segment and map all graphemes.
Comprehension: reread and point to text evidence.

basic.prompt: What are the first two sounds in flit?
What is the onset in flap?

conceptual.prompt: Why must reassessment items be fresh?
conceptual.answer: To check transfer instead of memorised answers.

conceptual.prompt: How many correct out of 15 meet 80%?

conceptual.answer: The component shown as weak by diagnostic evidence.

application.prompt: Correct “fag” when the target is flag.
Which practice helps a learner who omits l?
application.answer: Guided blending with sound boxes and fresh fl-words.

application.prompt: What route applies to 11 out of 15?

higherOrderThinking.prompt: How can you tell a decoding need from a comprehension need?
higherOrderThinking.answer: Check whether the word is read accurately and whether the learner uses text evidence.

higherOrderThinking.prompt: Why not repeat the same diagnostic questions?
higherOrderThinking.answer: The learner may remember answers without transferring the skill.

mixedReview.answer: Read it back and check each grapheme.
Exact words in the sentence or passage

activities.name: Select a practice path from diagnostic evidence.
steps: Model the specific sound, decoding, spelling, word-family or comprehension skill.
Practise with guided examples and immediate feedback.
Use fresh examples to check transfer.

activities.name: Complete a fresh reassessment and explain the route.
steps: Check responses against the answer key privately.
Calculate the score against the 80% threshold.
Advance or continue targeted remediation based on the score.

outcomes: Complete targeted practice matched to the diagnosed need.
Demonstrate transfer on fresh reassessment items.

questions.question: What are the first two phonemes in flit?
What is the rime in flag?
Which word has a different rime from flap?
Read: “The flag is on the mat.” Where is the flag?
Read: “Ben can flap the flag.” What can Ben do?
If flag is read as fag, what should the learner do?
options: Add a vowel between f and l

questions.question: What is the best fluency goal?
options: Read accurately and smoothly while keeping meaning

questions.question: What best supports a literal answer?
options: Point to the exact sentence words
Add a detail not in the text

questions.question: Why must reassessment use fresh items?
If a learner scores 11 out of 15, what happens next?
options: Continue targeted remediation because 11 is below 12/15
Repeat the same items until memorised

answerKeys.explanation: Flip ends in -ip; the other words share -ap.
The sentence states the flag is on the mat.
The sentence states that Ben can flap the flag.
The /l/ in the initial blend was omitted.
Fluency includes accuracy, smoothness and comprehension.
Literal answers should be supported by explicit text evidence.
Fresh items show whether the skill generalises.
Eleven is below the 80% mastery threshold.
